trigger: Approval store not open (permanent) or a transient SQLite failure during MCP approval recall: get_checked/consume_ticket now return kInternalError -32603, a code docs/user-manual/mcp.md does not document for this path.
summary: mcp.md has no -32603 entry for the approval recall path, and its only documented recall remediation (-32003: 'submit the call without approval_id to obtain a fresh approval ticket') is the OPPOSITE of the new permanent-arm body ('do NOT request a fresh one ... Escalate to an operator'). A client built to our own reference doc discards or duplicates a live human-approved capability on a maker-checker control. Raised INDEPENDENTLY by docs-writer and security-guardian in the same Gate 2 wave; the orchestrator separately confirmed by grep that mcp.md carries no approval-path -32603 and that the -32003 fix text reads as quoted.
classification_rationale: Required doc under item 2 (user-manual section for a changed operator workflow) and item 5 (error-code table). Absence, not wording.

trigger: A foreign-origin ticket is refused at recall and folded into the existing -32003 'already used' text by design (anti-oracle).
summary: Neither the -32003 cause list nor the step-6 recall-validation prose names the minting-surface condition, and neither points the operator at the audit-side discriminator 'refused: foreign_origin' which is the only way to tell a cross-surface refusal from an ordinary replay. Orchestrator confirmed step 6 enumerates only approved / matching tool+arguments / not-yet-consumed.
classification_rationale: A required user-manual list enumerated as closed that this change makes incomplete.

trigger: Release assembly of the Security section from the two 2442 fragments.
summary: This fragment is the one that actually causes the outstanding-ticket breakage on upgrade but carries no '**Breaking -**' lead-in; the label sits only on the sibling fragment.
classification_rationale: Presentation of an accurate fragment; no claim is false.

trigger: A future ApprovalManager::submit() call site that omits the defaulted origin argument.
summary: No repository-level home records that submit()'s origin defaults to the granting kUnspecified and that every new mint call site must pass it explicitly. Documented in-code at approval_manager.hpp:200-208, but in-code prose never satisfies a required-doc obligation. Recommended as one line on the existing ADR-1005 'approval gate' row.
classification_rationale: Item 4 - a new architectural invariant with no routed-concern or CLAUDE.md home.

trigger: A future ApprovalOrigin enumerator added without a to_string arm.
summary: to_string(ApprovalOrigin) has NO -Wswitch-as-error pragma, unlike its sibling consume_denial_reason which got one. A future enumerator without an arm falls through to return "", which decodes to kUnspecified - the value that GRANTS redemption. The fail-open function is the one without the build gate. Capped at NICE by E6 (all five enumerators are handled today, so the wrong outcome cannot occur now). Orchestrator confirmed the pragma is absent.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: A future mint call site that omits the origin argument.
summary: submit()'s origin parameter defaults to ApprovalOrigin::kUnspecified, which is the value that grants at redemption. All three production callers were grep-verified correct today, which is why E6 caps it; the hazard is prospective.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: Reading the kUnspecified doc comment to decide whether the MCP mint can declare kMcp.
summary: The kUnspecified doc comment says the MCP gate 'cannot be updated to declare kMcp while mcp_server.cpp is frozen for a parallel rebase'. This diff edits mcp_server.cpp (+46/-4) in that same handler, so the stated reason no longer holds. The prose pre-existed on origin/dev; this change is what falsified it. Prose adjacent to a control branch, so a truth finding rather than wording. Orchestrator verified both halves.
classification_rationale: In-code prose that contradicts the change shipping alongside it, adjacent to the origin control.

trigger: Approval store unavailable during an MCP recall.
summary: A store OUTAGE is audited result='denied' on the new branches, while the sibling approval-submit failure uses result='failure'. That pollutes the denial signal #2442 exists to produce: an infrastructure fault becomes indistinguishable from a refused redemption attempt in the denial counts.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: Any approval-store failure on the MCP recall path.
summary: appr_read.error() and consumed.error().message - the latter carrying sqlite3_errmsg text - are discarded: never logged, never audited. The operator diagnosing a wedged approval gate has no record of why the store failed.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: A reviewer inspecting an approval before approving it.
summary: GET /api/v1/approvals/{id} does not expose origin, so the human reviewer cannot see which surface minted the ticket - the very fact the changelog names as the threat. Defence-in-depth only now that redemption is guarded server-side; the file is untouched by this change.
classification_rationale: A read surface that omits a field, not a false statement.

trigger: Building on MSVC with a ConsumeFailure enumerator added but no consume_denial_reason arm.
summary: The header asserts 'Adding a ConsumeFailure without a token here FAILS THE BUILD'. The GCC/Clang half is VERIFIED - the orchestrator compiled a reduced case: missing arm gives error: enumeration value 'kNewKind' not handled in switch [-Werror=switch], exit 1, with a positive control at exit 0. The MSVC half is NOT: C4062 is off-by-default and whether #pragma warning(error : 4062) alone enables it is unestablished. Routed to cpp-expert in Gate 3. The overall claim still holds via the GCC/Clang CI legs, so it is not false as written - only unproven on one platform.
classification_rationale: A build-behaviour claim in prose whose truth on one supported platform is unestablished.

trigger: Audit sink failure while recording a foreign-origin refusal.
summary: mcp_audit's return bool is discarded at every site, so the foreign_origin detection row - the evidence #2442 exists to produce - can be lost silently. Pre-existing MCP set-and-proceed pattern, but nothing is actually set here.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

policy_floor: false-green test offered as closure evidence for a blocking finding
trigger: Removing migration v5's UPDATE statement and re-running [approval_manager].
summary: TEST_CASE 'migration v5 back-fills pre-existing rows to a fail-closed sentinel' cannot observe its own subject. MEASURED by mutation: deleting v5's UPDATE (leaving only ADD COLUMN) still passes 57/57 cases and 315/315 assertions, because the fixture starts schema_meta at v4 so create_tables runs v5, v6 AND v7 in one call, and v7's WHERE origin='' rewrites the same row to the same kUnrecognised outcome. The docstring's claim that it 'migrates v1..v5' is false. This test is the discriminating check for closure item A1 (the pre-v5 population - the actual #2442 attack), so it is closure evidence for a blocking finding that cannot fail when its subject is removed. Fix: cap schema_meta so v6/v7 do not also run, or isolate v5's effect. Related to but DISTINCT from ARCH-4, which is the same root cause seen as redundancy in the production migration.
classification_rationale: The test asserts a property of v5 that it cannot distinguish from v7's; the defect is in the test, not in prose.

trigger: A future revert of get_checked to get at the MCP approval recall.
summary: The store-error branch at the MCP recall has ZERO regression coverage. MEASURED by mutation: patching the branch to swallow a get_checked error into nullopt (reproducing the pre-fix get() semantics) passes the FULL server suite - 4661/4661 non-skipped cases, 235551/235551 assertions, zero failures. Every approval store-error test drives ApprovalManager or approval_store_error_body directly, never through the handler, and test_mcp_server.cpp references neither get_checked nor approval_store_error_body. RECORDED DISAGREEMENT: the reporter derived I1/E3 (HIGH, gating) and then labelled it SHOULD citing the missing-test-is-SHOULD rule; per the read rule the finding is taken at the stronger of the derived band and the label's floor, so it gates. The recorder notes the IMPACT is contestable because the production code is correct and only the guard is absent - the disposition is to FIX rather than adjudicate the band, which moots the question.
classification_rationale: Absent regression coverage for a branch the change exists to add.

trigger: A constant-value change to the transient retry hint.
summary: approval_store_error_body's transient retry_after_ms (5000) is asserted only as > 0, so a constant-value mutant survives. Pin the value for A5 honesty.
classification_rationale: Missing assertion precision, not a false statement.

trigger: Landing the Phase-2 REST approval redemption promised by the A4 schema at rest_api_v1.cpp:627.
summary: declares_non_mcp_surface encodes 'MCP is the sole redeemer' rather than 'the redeemer must match the minter'. There are already TWO redemption sinks: consume_ticket (guarded) and ScheduleRunner's query(approved)+fire_with_approval, which is bound instead by a.schedule_id == s.id and sits entirely outside the new predicate. When the REST gate's promised Phase-2 redemption lands it must call consume_ticket, which now unconditionally refuses kInstruction. ADR-1005 is satisfied today (the primitive is narrowed, not forked) but the shape blocks the next step. Suggested: have consume_ticket take the redeeming surface and refuse when origin != redeemer && origin != kUnspecified. RECORDED DISAGREEMENT: facts derive INFO, reporter labelled SHOULD; read at the stronger per the read rule.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: A future author adding an origin filter as a second copy in a SQL WHERE clause.
summary: The new single-chokepoint rule ('a copy in a WHERE clause is a second home ... the two would drift') exists only as a code comment. This is the same class as dispatch_target_shape.hpp and dangerous_enforce_in_spec, both of which carry a routed-concern row naming them catastrophic-if-forked. It should be recorded as such, together with the two-sink fact from ARCH-1 which no comment states.
classification_rationale: Item 4 - a new architectural invariant with no CLAUDE.md or routed-concern home.

trigger: Reading docs/postgres-migration-ladder.md to find which server stores remain on SQLite.
summary: ApprovalManager appears nowhere in the ladder (grep -c -i approval returns 0) while this change deepens it by two migrations. Its tables ride instructions.db via instr_db_pool_, so the ladder's InstructionStore row silently owns them - the same undocumented cohabitation the ladder's Notes record for SCIM on auth.db. Not the new-SQLite-store policy floor (the store is pre-existing), but the ADR-0006 row names the ladder as the ordered queue, so it accrues an entry per change.
classification_rationale: An author-facing doc a routed-concern row names as an update obligation.

trigger: Two databases both stamped schema_meta.version = 5 holding different data states.
summary: The in-place edit of shipped migration v5 is entirely redundant with v7 and costs the version-to-schema mapping. v5 runs only on a database below v5 (migration_runner.cpp:94, 'if (m.version <= current) continue;'), and in that case v7 runs immediately after in the same loop with no application write between; v5's ADD COLUMN ... DEFAULT '' leaves every pre-existing row at '', which is exactly the set v7's WHERE origin='' matches. Identical outcome, and editing a numbered migration means version 5 no longer identifies one data state. Recommend reverting v5 to its origin/dev form and keeping v7 alone. Orchestrator independently confirmed the runner semantics and the two statements. Converges with QA-2, which measured the same redundancy from the test side.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: Locating the file that owns the MCP approval error body.
summary: Layering is correct (mcp -> store, no cycle, nothing in the store includes it) and the template is the right seam, but the filename asserts store ownership while the content is namespace yuzu::server::mcp and pulls mcp_jsonrpc.hpp. Rename to mcp_approval_error.hpp.
classification_rationale: A naming choice; no behaviour and no false claim.

trigger: to_string(kUnrecognised) reached by any future write path.
summary: kUnrecognised's never-written invariant is convention-only: to_string(kUnrecognised) returns '' which decodes back to kUnspecified, the granting value. Distinct from SEC-2 (missing pragma) - this is the type shape. A decode-only value should not be expressible in the write path; return std::optional<ApprovalOrigin> from the decode, or give to_string a narrower writable enum. Separately: when a genuinely new surface is added, an older binary decodes it kUnrecognised and refuses - fail-closed and correct, but a rolling upgrade silently stops redeeming and nothing documents that.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: Any MSVC compile of a TU including approval_manager.hpp.
summary: SETTLES SEC-8. The MSVC arm is INERT and the header's 'FAILS THE BUILD' claim is false on MSVC. Microsoft's warning-pragma documentation attaches 'also turns on a warning that is off by default' to the 1|2|3|4 and default specifiers ONLY; for error: it says merely 'report the specified warnings as errors'. The off-by-default enable mechanisms are listed exhaustively elsewhere and #pragma warning(error : N) is not among them; C4062 is documented level 4, off. C4062 (not C4061) is the right number - this switch has no default label. Fix: precede with a level-independent enable, #pragma warning(1 : 4062). Unresolved secondary caveat: MSVC documents that the last warning-pragma setting in a function body applies to the whole function, so the in-function pop may undo the promotion regardless - either hoist the pragma outside the function or narrow the comment. I6(a) false-assurance was considered and rejected: the build-fail outcome still holds via the GCC/Clang Tier-1 legs, which the orchestrator verified by compiling a reduced case in both directions.
classification_rationale: In-code prose making a build-behaviour claim that is false on one supported platform.

trigger: Passing a callable whose fourth parameter is not numeric.
summary: approval_store_error_body requires BOTH a4_error(int, sv, sv) and a4_error(int, sv, sv, long); that implicit interface is documented nowhere and is hand-replicated at three sites. std::function cannot replace the template (the production a4_error carries default arguments that std::function erases), so the template is right - but add a requires clause or name both call shapes in a comment. The template has vague linkage, so inline is redundant and ODR is safe.
classification_rationale: An undocumented implicit template interface.

trigger: A concurrent writer causing SQLITE_BUSY partway through the find_pending walk.
summary: The while (sqlite3_step(...) == SQLITE_ROW) loop treats every non-SQLITE_ROW result as 'no more rows', so SQLITE_BUSY and SQLITE_ERROR are indistinguishable from a clean SQLITE_DONE. The conflation is pre-existing, but removing LIMIT 1 WIDENS it: a truncated walk now returns nullopt while a redeemable older candidate exists further down, and the mint then creates a duplicate pending ticket. Capture the final rc and treat non-SQLITE_DONE distinctly. A reviewer could argue I3 (the caller cannot tell nullopt-means-none from nullopt-means-failed); recorded, but the system outcome is a duplicate ticket, not a grant or a burn.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: An open SQLite handle whose reads fail permanently - SQLITE_CORRUPT, SQLITE_NOTADB, SQLITE_READONLY on a read-only volume, or SQLITE_FULL.
summary: is_open() returns db_ != nullptr and db_ is written only at boot, so the classifier reads a boot-time fact rather than the state of the read that just failed. Every open-handle permanent failure therefore takes the TRANSIENT arm and directs an unbounded retry, each attempt writing an audit row - an audit-write loop on the substrate already failing to serve it. The header documents its own non-exhaustiveness honestly, but the derivation still lands at MEDIUM. Closing it properly means classifying on sqlite3_extended_errcode carried in ConsumeError.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: std::bad_alloc thrown by col_text or push_back between sqlite3_step and sqlite3_finalize.
summary: Nine manual prepare/finalize pairs remain in functions this diff touches (:313,344,357,434,467,485,512,696,748). Every early return was checked and all are hand-balanced with no leak, including submit's queue-full return at :318. But std::string construction between step and finalize can throw, leaking the statement and - because the connection is closed with close_v2 - pinning it as a zombie. Pre-existing in a touched file, so SHOULD per the preamble narrowing rather than the policy floor. Convert to SqliteStmt as each is next edited; find_pending is now the correct pattern.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: A concurrent consume or expiry between the origin guard's get_checked and the CAS UPDATE.
summary: The recall is now two separate mtx_ acquisitions (guard read, then CAS), which is a TOCTOU window - but NOT exploitable. Verified that origin has no runtime writer: grep 'UPDATE approvals' yields only migrations v5/v7 (boot-only) plus status/consumed_at/review columns. Origin is write-once at insert, so it cannot change mid-flight; the window admits only expiry or a concurrent consume, both of which make the CAS decline. Cost is one extra lock and prepare round trip.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: 1000 pending rows sharing one (definition_id, submitted_by, scope_expression) key, all declaring a non-MCP surface.
summary: PREMISE REFUTED, and this narrows rather than confirms the concern. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN is byte-identical with and without LIMIT 1 in both distributions measured on a synthetic 1M-row table: LIMIT 1 never avoided the sort, and where the v6 index idx_approvals_status_submitted is chosen the ORDER BY is index-covered with or without it. The added cost is purely C++ row materialisation, measured 1.15 ms vs 0.01 ms across 1000 rows, and the walk is already bounded by kMaxPendingApprovals = 1000 (:309). Worst case is self-inflictable because the REST mint has no per-submitter cap (MCP's 25-cap is checked AFTER find_pending). Suggested belt-and-braces: append LIMIT 1000, equal to the existing cap so it is provably semantics-free today.
classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.

trigger: Ordinary operation over time.
summary: The approvals table never deletes - grep finds no DELETE FROM approvals anywhere. Status flips pending to approved/rejected/expired and consumed rows keep status='approved', so growth is unbounded and permanent. Not introduced here (the v6 comment already concedes nothing prunes), but this change couples boot cost to it via the v5/v7 full-table writes. Any future sweep lands squarely in the clock-guarded-retention routed concern - persisted anchor, fact-set dedup, unconditional cap - which is correctly NOT matched by this diff.
classification_rationale: A missing retention mechanism, not a false statement.
A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: Any sqlite3_prepare_v2 failure inside ApprovalManager::query.
summary: query() has no error channel - orchestrator confirmed it returns the empty results vector on prepare failure. The schedule runner therefore reads a store failure as 'no approval exists': fire_with_approval misses a live approved ticket, misses the pending one, and mints a DUPLICATE ask every tick. This is the identical class the PR fixes at get->get_checked, still open on the sibling redemption sink. Converges with CONS-1.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: One submitted_by accumulating more than 100 approval rows newer than an approved ticket.
summary: query()'s ORDER BY submitted_at DESC LIMIT 100 (orchestrator confirmed at :432) combined with never-pruned rows permanently wedges a schedule. consume_ticket's CAS sets consumed_at only - status stays 'approved' - and nothing deletes (PERF-2). Once 100 newer rows exist for that owner, query({status:approved}) can no longer return the ticket; the schedule holds at due forever, re-asking, with no error anywhere. I5 raised to HIGH: it wedges a state machine.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: SQLITE_BUSY on an open handle driving the transient arm's retry hint.
summary: retry_after_ms: 5000 is a self-sustaining feedback loop. Nothing enforces the delay, nothing circuit-breaks. N clients retrying contend the same mtx_ AND the same shared instr_db_pool_ connection the instruction store, schedule engine and approval gate serialise on, so the retries sustain the busy condition that caused them. I5 raised: unbounded, on a serialised path shared with an enforcement operation. Converges with SRE-2.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: A store outage lasting longer than the ticket's remaining 7-day TTL.
summary: The permanent arm tells the caller 'the approval was not consumed and stays valid once the store is restored - do not request a fresh one. Escalate to an operator.' On restore the next submit() sweep expires the ticket and the recall answers 'already used'. The operator follows the escalation instruction and waits on a capability that has been silently retired. I4: a named action that conceals the real state.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: An idle server, or one whose mint path is failing, holding approved-unconsumed tickets.
summary: The 7-day TTL is enforced ONLY by the lazy sweep inside submit() - orchestrator confirmed the in-code comment reads 'Lazy expiry sweep (runs on every mint, under mtx_)'. A server that is not minting never expires anything, so approved-unconsumed one-time capabilities outlive their stated TTL indefinitely - the exact leak the sweep's own comment says it exists to prevent. NOTE: this is the subject of the PARKED PR 2 ('enforce the 7-day window AT REDEMPTION'), which the rebuild ladder already assigns it to.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: A concurrent submit() sweep expiring a ticket between the guard read and the CAS.
summary: The sweep races the now three-acquisition recall, producing an intermittent 'approval already used' on a ticket never consumed. Widened window only; remediation still correct.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: A store failure while an agentic worker polls the A4 status_url target.
summary: GET /api/v1/approvals/{id} calls get(), which masks a store failure as 404 'approval not found'. Same defect the PR fixes one file over. Orchestrator confirmed this is the ONLY remaining get() caller in server/core/src. Converges with CONS-1, which adds that it also contradicts the published OpenAPI reserving 503 for this condition.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: Restarting on an older binary against a database already migrated to v7.
summary: MigrationRunner skips m.version <= current and never REFUSES a database newer than the binary. An older server opens the v7 database, decodes 'legacy' as kUnspecified - the granting value - with no log line. The 'rollback loses the fix' half is tautological; the absence of DETECTION is not. Flagged for adjudication. NOTE sre separately verified the rollback is otherwise inert (dev's consume_ticket has no origin check at all).

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: Upgrade boot against a large approvals table.
summary: v5+v7 rewrite every row under BEGIN IMMEDIATE on instructions.db, a table that never prunes: boot stall, WAL growth proportional to table size, write lock held against every co-tenant store. performance measured 371 ms + 64 ms at 1M rows; sre found no startup-budget gate that this threatens today.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: An operator trying to confirm the upgrade note's diagnosis from the API.
summary: GET /api/v1/approvals/{id} exposes neither origin nor consumed_at, so a refused-but-unconsumed ticket is indistinguishable from a spent one. The upgrade note redirects to the audit row, which sits behind a different permission. Extends SEC-7/CONS-5.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: REST-minted mcp.-prefixed tickets accumulating under an MCP dedup key.
summary: Removing the mint-time refusal lets the REST gate mint mcp.-prefixed rows that find_pending skips forever. They count against the GLOBAL 1000 pending cap, whose exhaustion makes fire_with_approval fail and ADVANCE the schedule - occurrences silently skipped fleet-wide.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: A prepare failure on the pending-cap count query.
summary: The 1000-pending cap is enforced only inside if (prepare == SQLITE_OK), so it fails OPEN on a prepare failure.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: Starting the new binary while the old process still holds writes.
summary: Rolling restart can refuse boot: v5's BEGIN IMMEDIATE hits SQLITE_BUSY, the migration fails, create_tables fails closed and the server will not start.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: An operator needing to inspect a wedged approval store inside a shipped image.
summary: No sqlite3 CLI ships in any artifact. Converges with SRE-3, which verified all four packaging targets.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: Deleting a schedule that owns an approved, unconsumed ticket.
summary: delete_schedule does not cascade and no DELETE FROM approvals exists, so the orphaned ticket stays approved/consumed_at=0 until a sweep runs, feeding UP-2's window.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: A client re-asking after each rejection.
summary: find_pending matches status='pending' only, so a rejected request is not dedup'd and the client re-asks indefinitely with no backoff.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: A prepare/step failure on an open approvals handle while a worker polls GET /api/v1/approvals/{id}.
summary: The store-error-collapses-to-absence SINK is fixed at 2 sites and left at 3. GET /api/v1/approvals/{id} - the A4 status_url target an agentic worker polls - still calls get() and answers a store failure with 404, contradicting the published OpenAPI at rest_api_v1.cpp:911 which reserves 503 for 'approval store not initialised' and defines 404 as 'no approval matches the id'. query() is the same sink at three more sites. The consistency point: this PR DELETED the 2-arg consume_ticket overload precisely because a future caller would lose the distinction, then left get() in place with one of its callers already wrong - fixing the instance, not the sink. Orchestrator confirmed rest_api_v1.cpp:5854 is the only remaining get() caller.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: An MCP approval submit failing on a store error or the pending cap.
summary: approval_store_error.hpp asserts that omitting retry_after_ms is A4's encoding for 'not retryable', and docs/agentic-first-principle.md:83 agrees. The sibling kInternalError 80 lines above in the same handler is retryable in prose ('retry later') and encodes null. The new code defines the encoding; its neighbour falsifies it.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: #2443 wiring a non-empty ConsumePrecondition at mcp_server.cpp:3366.
summary: The ConsumeFailure-to-response classifier is an if, not a switch, so it has no gate at all - the closed-set claim is enforced only for the AUDIT token. kPrecondition (documented 'ticket UNTOUCHED, still recallable') would map to 'approval already used (one-time ticket)'. Capped LOW by E6: {} is passed literally today so kPrecondition is unproducible. Distinct from the settled C4062 item.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: An operator following server-admin.md:360 to find refusal rows.
summary: The denial audit emits 'approval <id> refused: <token>' while every sibling uses the approval_id=<id> key (mcp_server.cpp:3271,3303; workflow_routes.cpp:1567; schedule_runner.cpp:147,172). The upgrade note now tells operators to find these rows, so the correlation key matters.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: An approver deciding whether a ticket is worth reviewing.
summary: origin is invisible on BOTH read surfaces - extends SEC-7 to list_pending_approvals and the OpenAPI Approval schema at rest_api_v1.cpp:634. The fact this PR records is readable only from the audit trail, so an approver cannot see that a kUnrecognised ticket is already dead before spending a review on it.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: An authenticated MCP session redeeming a ticket minted by a different surface.
summary: No Prometheus counter for the event this PR exists to detect. Orchestrator confirmed zero metric references anywhere in the diff. kForeignOrigin is recorded ONLY as an audit-row detail string via mcp_audit, whose nodiscard bool is discarded at every site (SEC-9). docs/observability-conventions.md establishes the platform's own pattern for security-relevant refusals - metric as SIEM signal, audit row as forensic evidence (peer_mismatch_total, lockout_applied_total, breakglass_login_total). This ships with only the evidence half, so there is no alertable channel for cross-surface forgery attempts at all. I6 with E2: the actor is using a human approval granted for another surface.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: A SQLite handle open but permanently unusable after boot.
summary: Degraded-but-open store: unbounded retry compounds into unbounded audit writes with no circuit breaker. Every recall is served retry_after_ms 5000 with no server-side backoff, and every failed attempt writes an audit row. /readyz's approval_manager check (verified present at server.cpp:7977, pre-existing) reads the same boot-time is_open(), so it stays GREEN through exactly this failure mode - indefinite 5s-interval audit-write load with no operator lever and no green-to-red signal to page on. Builds on SAFE-1; converges with UP-3.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: An operator following the documented boot-wedge recovery procedure.
summary: The wedged-schema runbook depends on a binary absent from every shipped artifact. Verified directly: Dockerfile.server and Dockerfile.server.chisel both dropped libsqlite3-0/the sqlite chisel slice and neither installs the sqlite3 CLI; debian/control depends only on shlibs/misc/adduser; the RPM spec has no sqlite Requires. Yet server-admin.md:1063-1075 and upgrading.md prescribe docker exec ... sqlite3 against instructions.db - the same file this PR's migrations touch. This PR adds no new sqlite3-dependent step, but adds no remediation for a wedged v5/v7 migration either, so the only documented path fails with command-not-found in every shipped target.

classification_rationale: A defect in code, not prose.
trigger: An operator with an outstanding approval and no mcp.-prefixed definitions skim-reading the upgrade section.
